prompt.zh-TW: 河岸麵包坊的麵粉供應商這個月延遲交貨，依合約付給麵包坊 {{money:vars.penalty}} 的違約金。這筆收益該怎麼看？
prompt.en: This month Riverside Bakery’s flour supplier delivered late and, under the contract, paid the bakery a penalty of {{money:vars.penalty}}. How should this income be viewed?

text.zh-TW: 業外的一次性收益，不算麵包坊本業的成績
text.en: A one-off gain outside the core business, not part of the bakery’s trading performance

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。麵包坊的本業是賣麵包；違約金是供應商出狀況才有的錢，要和營業收入分開看。
feedback.en: That’s right. The bakery’s business is selling bread; the penalty only arrived because the supplier slipped up, so it is kept apart from revenue.

text.zh-TW: 營業收入的一部分，因為錢是麵包坊收到的
text.en: Part of revenue, because the bakery received the money

feedback.zh-TW: 錢確實進了麵包坊，這點沒錯。但營業收入只算賣麵包賺的；違約金不是客人買麵包付的錢，混進去會讓人以為生意比實際好。
feedback.en: The money did reach the bakery, that much is right. But revenue counts only what is earned by selling bread; a penalty is not money customers paid for bread, and mixing it in would make the business look better than it is.

text.zh-TW: 每個月都能期待的經常性收益
text.en: A recurring gain to expect every month

feedback.zh-TW: 你想到了「以後還會不會有」，這個問題問得對。不過供應商不會每個月都延遲交貨；這筆錢是對方出狀況才有的，一次性的收益不能當成每月的常態。
feedback.en: You asked whether it will come again, and that is the right question. But the supplier will not deliver late every month; this money arrived only because something went wrong, and a one-off gain cannot be treated as the monthly norm.

explanation.zh-TW: 讀損益表時要問兩件事：這筆是本業還是業外？是經常有還是一次性的？供應商付的違約金兩個答案都是後者，所以是{{option:o_s0mt}}。{{option:o_78gj}}把它混進本業，{{option:o_qvs1}}把它當成常態。
explanation.en: When reading an income statement, ask two things: is this item from the core business or outside it, and is it recurring or one-off? A supplier’s penalty payment is the latter on both counts, so {{option:o_s0mt}} is right. {{option:o_78gj}} mixes it into the core business and {{option:o_qvs1}} treats it as the norm.
